title: Not a scam, works great!
body: Overall I love this app. The interface and functionality could be improved but it does what it says it does. I purchased this app in summer 2025 and figured I’d try it for a year and see if it was worth it. I fly about once a month. I meticulously use google flights to track flight prices and will call the airline for a refund if I see the price go down. What I don’t like about google flights is you can’t set the alerts to notify you if it goes below a certain price. It will email you every time the price changes so this method pretty much requires constant monitoring to know when to call and you might miss the window if you don’t check before the price has gone up again. This app automates that whole process. For me that has been 100% worth it just for the time and effort saved. The cons: it works better for some airlines than others. I’ve successfully gotten credits from delta, United, and southwest. JetBlue, while you can add it to Jetpack, they require you to share your JetBlue login info (username and password) and 2FA with JetBack in order for them to get you your credit. I’m assuming this has more to do with the JetBlue process than Jetpack. But regardless, I don’t feel comfortable sharing my 2FA with this app so it basically doesn’t work for JetBlue. I’ve also noticed that it doesn’t work as well for multi city itineraries or flights booked with points. That said, I kept my google flight tracking and this app never missed a dip in price and even got some that didn’t show up on google flights. Suggestions: I wish the interface has a bit more info. It will just tell you which flights it’s tracking and money recovered. I wish I could click on each flight and see how the price has changed over time like I can on google flights. Summary: this app was worth it for me. I got $193 back in credit over the past 6 months. I’m pretty good at tracking flight prices and buying them when they’re already low, so if you’re not doing that you’ll probably get back more. For me it’s worth the reduced effort so long as I’m net positive.
